correctness.rationale: The upper-bound matrices yield exactly \(1-2(i-j)^2\) and \(2(j-i)-1\) at every pair, so strict signs are correct for every positive chain length. Every triple in dimension at most two meeting the equality sign pattern must have a strictly positive linear dependence: zero coefficients would force forbidden collinearity, and mixed signs would force a positive diagonal to equal a negative combination of off-diagonal scores. The all-negative first column of strict order contradicts that positive dependence. Separate arguments establish the exact minima for one and two entities. The bundled integer verifier passed all 338350 ordered-pair cases through size 100 and 18 separate three-point comparisons; finite testing is not used as the universal proof.

value.rationale: Equality and strict linear order are canonical logical relations on finite chains. When atomic truth is read by the signs of bilinear scores, every domain size has a shared dimension-three solution, as opposed to the size-dependent dimension required for exact matrix entries. Three elements is a meaningful sharp interaction boundary: each relation alone has a two-dimensional signed representation, but no shared two-dimensional carrier can accommodate both. This exact resource invariant isolates a constraint relevant to multi-relational representation design, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It does not claim downstream quantifier or modal correctness.
